source: src/bin/Data/Item and armor-part models in src/bin/Data/Player

scope.selection: Core weapon, shield, bow, staff, spellbook and wing filename families plus named special models from OpenItems; player armor component filename families, including class base parts, variants and nested LuckyItem set models.

quality_scores.reason: 9 models; 38–112 triangles (60 median), mostly 32–64 px maps. Early axes have thin, blocky heads and little grip separation. UV screen flags exist; inspect the individual maps before changing them. UV screen: 30/432 analyzed triangles (6.94%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

24 bow/crossbow models; 58–783 triangles (217 median), with 32 px shared support maps common in the early bows. The first bow has a narrow, angular outline and low-resolution texture. Some UV islands screen above 8:1 anisotropy. UV screen: 364/6429 analyzed triangles (5.66%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

2 arrow models; 42–75 triangles and sub-128 px maps. Their silhouettes are readable but very simple; tiny shafts and fletching make texture stretch worth checking at game scale. UV screen: 7/101 analyzed triangles (6.93%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

22 models; 36–1194 triangles (395 median). Early examples include Mace02 at 118 triangles with a 16×16 map and Mace01 at 36 triangles with a 32×32 map. The heads lack rounded volume and clear material breaks. UV screen: 279/9177 analyzed triangles (3.04%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

22 models; 18–408 triangles (84 median), and low-resolution maps are common. Shield01 has 18 triangles and a 32×32 map; the first shield reads as a thin, flat plate. UV outliers should be reviewed in context. UV screen: 81/2909 analyzed triangles (2.78%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

11 models; 46–162 triangles (112 median), with 32×16 to 128×32 maps represented. Early profiles are narrow and spare; edge bevels, socket transitions and material breaks need painted or geometric emphasis. UV screen: 42/944 analyzed triangles (4.45%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

22 models; 16 triangles median and all referenced textures have a side below 128 px. Nineteen models share the same 64×64 book.OZJ; geometry and the shared cover art offer unusually high reuse leverage. UV anisotropy screening is elevated for this family. UV screen: 44/638 analyzed triangles (6.9%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

29 models; 50–1360 triangles (462 median), with early 16–64 px maps and several tiny glow/support maps. Staff02 is 50 triangles with 32×32 and 16×16 maps. Orbs and head pieces need stronger silhouettes and value separation. UV screen: 663/12937 analyzed triangles (5.12%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

44 models; 24–584 triangles (243.5 median). Many early maps have a 16–64 px short side; Sword03 is 49 triangles with a 32×32 map. Blade profiles, guard thickness and grip/pommel readability are the main silhouette opportunities. UV screen: 232/10396 analyzed triangles (2.23%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

3 models; 16–46 triangles (32 median). Wing01 is only 16 triangles despite a 64×64 map; the preview confirms a flat, sparse silhouette. Gen1 wings need the most substantial shape and texture rework. UV screen: 0/94 analyzed triangles (0.0%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

4 models; 102–872 triangles (390 median), mostly 64–128 px maps. Articulated outlines improve over Gen1, but the representative remains angular and the 64×32 Wing07 map is undersized for its broad surface. UV screen: 24/1754 analyzed triangles (1.37%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

4 models; 274–1842 triangles (995 median), with 128–256 px maps on the main forms. Shape and detail are stronger than earlier generations, but Wing08 exceeds the 1500-triangle item target and the Blender preview shows dark regions that need an in-client alpha/render check. UV screen: 53/4053 analyzed triangles (1.31%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

11 cape, robe and shop-wing models; 16–874 triangles (192 median) and mixed 64–256 px maps. Quality is uneven; several robes and early store wings have flat folded silhouettes. Preserve their alpha and scrolling behavior when retouching. UV screen: 4/2700 analyzed triangles (0.15%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

97 models; 120–1414 triangles (352 median), with both 128–256 px body maps and tiny hide/overlay maps. The sampled sets range from basic blocky plates to more ornate layered pieces. UV screen: 613/38385 analyzed triangles (1.6%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

94 models; 106–676 triangles (190 median); 89 of 106 texture references have a side below 128 px. Boot UV screening has the highest median model p95 anisotropy of the armor parts; inspect flagged triangles for degeneracy before editing. UV screen: 795/19993 analyzed triangles (3.98%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

85 models; 130–492 triangles (180 median); most maps are 64–128 px. The sampled set reads at a distance, but glove seams and raised knuckle forms rely on small painted details. UV screen: 617/17405 analyzed triangles (3.54%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

92 models; 38–638 triangles (197 median), with many 32–64 px face/trim maps alongside larger skin maps. Some silhouettes are distinctive, while low-triangle helmets and shared hair/skin maps limit finish. UV screen: 488/21983 analyzed triangles (2.22%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

95 models; 84–636 triangles (142 median); many maps are 32–128 px and some 2×2 hide maps are engine placeholders. Cloth folds and armor/cloth boundaries often need stronger shape or paint definition. UV screen: 476/19494 analyzed triangles (2.44%) exceed 8:1 anisotropy; this flags inspection, not confirmed visible stretching.

18 triangles with a 32×32 map; the preview shows a very flat starter shield silhouette.
16 triangles with a 64×64 map; the Gen1 preview has the weakest silhouette and very little surface structure.
58 triangles and two 32×32 maps; the string, limbs and grip need stronger shape and contrast.
48 triangles and one 32×32 map; head thickness and blade-to-haft separation are limited.
46 triangles with a 32×32 map; the long, narrow form benefits from stronger tip, socket and grip definition.
50 triangles with 32×32 and 16×16 maps; the head/orb treatment is constrained by low-resolution maps.
36 triangles and a 32×32 map; the compact head and shaft have little modeled volume.
49 triangles with a 32×32 map; blade profile, guard and handle read as one thin, low-detail form.
Book01–Book19 each use 16-triangle geometry and share Item/book.OZJ (64×64 across 19 models), so one coordinated redesign improves a whole family.
26 triangles and a 32×32 map; reinforce rim, boss and handle-side thickness without changing attachment placement.
72 triangles; its main map is 64×16 and the secondary 2×2 texture is a placeholder-sized reference. Check mesh flags before consolidating.
60 triangles with a 32×32 map; low geometry and a small map constrain its blade and shaft transitions.
76 triangles; the main map is 64×64 and its two shared support maps are 32×32. The limbs, grip and string need clearer construction.
60 triangles and one 32×32 map; enlarge the read of the edge, cheek and haft while retaining the current origin.
68 triangles with a 64×64 map; a small UV anisotropy screen outlier accompanies a basic silhouette, so inspect mapping before rebuilding.
66 triangles with two 32×16 maps; the low short side and narrow texture allocation make blade highlights and grip detail difficult.
268 triangles with a 64×32 map; broad wing surfaces deserve better texel allocation and a clearer feather/energy silhouette.
The sampled five parts total 706 triangles. Individual armor/boot/glove/helm/pant maps are mostly 32–128 px; rework as a coordinated set and preserve player skeleton/action bindings.
The sampled five parts total 616 triangles, with mostly 64–128 px garment maps. Improve class silhouette and material separation across all five parts as one set.

style_guide.intent: A coherent, hand-painted MU fantasy style: large readable forms, deliberate silhouette, restrained highlights and class identity. This is a proposal for future item-art requests, not a change to existing asset behavior.

materials.treatment: Single diffuse map; broad mid-tone planes, painted bevel highlights and contact shadows; separate edge, face and rivet values without PBR maps.
Warm restrained browns, directional grain painted at readable scale, dark seam and grip transitions.
Distinct broad folds or feather groups, clear value grouping, alpha only where the source material already needs it.
Small high-saturation accent, bright center and painted rim/glow; keep the base silhouette readable without bloom.

geometry_budget_triangles_per_bmd.weapons_sword_axe_mace_spear: 250–900 typical; spend toward the top only for a visibly better silhouette or construction.
geometry_budget_triangles_per_bmd.bow_staff_shield: 300–1000 typical; preserve readable string, grip, shaft, rim and attachment details.
geometry_budget_triangles_per_bmd.wings: 500–1500; reserve geometry for the outline and large feather/energy forms. Wing08's current 1842 is above the item-art target and should be optimized if reworked.
geometry_budget_triangles_per_bmd.armour_parts: 150–500 typical for each of the five part BMDs; keep every individual model at or below 1500 and budget the set together.
geometry_budget_triangles_per_bmd.engine_hard_ceiling: The asset pipeline validator rejects more than 15000 triangles, but the stricter 1500 item-art limit from Item Editor plan section 2 is the design ceiling.

texture_budget.common: 256×256 diffuse for important surfaces; 128×128 where surface area/detail is modest.
texture_budget.hero: 512×512 when the model's screen area and paint detail justify it.
texture_budget.exception: 1024×1024 maximum only for a large/high-impact asset where UV allocation benefits; do not upscale as a substitute for clean UVs.
texture_budget.format_and_layout: Power-of-two dimensions, maximum 1024×1024; one texture per mesh, one UV set. Keep render suffixes _R/_H/_S/_N and mesh order. Use an atlas when a single mesh needs multiple painted material looks.

style_checks: readable at inventory and equipped scale
one dominant silhouette cue per asset
paint material separation into the supported diffuse texture
use geometry for primary shape, texture for small surface detail

risks.risk: Shared textures can change many models at once.
risks.evidence: 131 shared texture files in scope; Player/hide.OZJ is referenced by 102 models, Item/book.OZJ by 19, Player/hide_m.OZJ by 19 and Item/bow01.OZJ by 9.
risks.mitigation: Use the per-texture model list in shared_textures before repainting; make shared changes only after checking every consumer. Prefer a new uniquely named map only when mesh/material behavior permits.

risks.risk: Attachment origin, orientation and scale control equipped placement.
risks.evidence: Hands, back and shields attach through model origin; game-side angles are hard-coded. Preview renders recenter each model for display, so their visual placement does not validate the original pivot.
risks.mitigation: Preserve the original pivot/orientation/scale, record raw bind-pose bounds, and compare equipped/inventory placement in the client before acceptance.

risks.risk: Mesh order and texture suffixes carry runtime behavior.
risks.evidence: The engine hides or blends item meshes by index; _R, _H, _S and _N suffixes select render flags. Export can merge meshes that share a texture name.
risks.mitigation: Preserve mesh count/order and per-mesh texture/flags; compare `bmdconv info` before/after and validate each exported BMD.

risks.risk: Armor has skeleton and action compatibility requirements.
risks.evidence: Player armor component models bind to the player skeleton; imported armor data records bones/actions and their ordering.
risks.mitigation: Keep the Player skeleton, bone order and every action for armor changes; use `bmdconv compare` against the source.

risks.risk: The offline Blender material/alpha preview can differ from the game renderer.
risks.evidence: Wing Gen3's preview contains large dark regions; preview is offline and uses the repository BMD importer.
risks.mitigation: Inspect source texture alpha and flags, then confirm questionable alpha/glow behavior in the client.

previews.lighting: shared 3-area-light neutral studio with fixed positions and energies
previews.renderer: Blender Cycles, offline, source models imported with tools/blender/mu_bmd_import.py; no animation used.

uv_stretch_method: Per-triangle SMD tangent-space Jacobian singular-value ratio after scaling UVs to texture pixels; ratios describe anisotropy, not a standalone art-quality verdict.

assessment_method.quality_scale: 1 = largest quality gap, 3 = mixed/usable baseline, 5 = little rework indicated; scores are an art-direction assessment, not an engine-validity grade.
assessment_method.uv_screen: Per-triangle UV anisotropy from bmdconv BMD-to-SMD geometry/UV data. Ratios above 8:1 are review flags only; near-degenerate geometry can produce outliers and every flag requires visual inspection.
assessment_method.candidate_order: Ranked by expected visual lift from baseline: weak silhouette/low triangle count, small texture dimensions, and shared-family reuse. Armor rows are coordinated five-part set targets. This is a model-level shortlist, not an item-ID catalog.
assessment_method.texture_sharing: Shared texture records are derived from model texture references and same-folder resolution; case/extension alternatives are recorded on each texture entry.
